problem.title: Frankl half-frequency conclusion for union-closures of linear 3-uniform generating systems
problem.informal_statement: Freeze one exactly defined structural subclass of finite union-closed families and claim the Frankl half-frequency conclusion for it. The class is the union-closure of a linear 3-uniform generating system: m >= 1 pairwise distinct 3-element sets whose pairwise intersections have size at most one. The family F consists of the unions of all subfamilies of the generating system, so the empty set (the empty union) is a member and is counted in |F|. The claim is that some element of the ground set lies in at least half the members of F. Both a proof for the frozen class and an exact finite counterexample inside it are acceptable outcomes; a counterexample inside the class would also refute the headline conjecture. The full Frankl conjecture is not the target. Novelty of the frozen class is not_assessed: whether this class is already covered by a published special case is an untrusted status question and an acquisition target, not a claim of this dossier.

target_claim.statement: For every integer m >= 1 and every family G = {A_1, ..., A_m} of m pairwise distinct 3-element finite sets satisfying |A_i intersect A_j| <= 1 for all i != j, let F = { union of A_i over i in S : S subset of {1,...,m} } and let U(F) be the union of all members of F. Then there exists x in U(F) such that 2 * card({A in F : x in A}) >= card(F), where card(F) is the number of distinct members of F and counts the empty set, which is the union over S = empty.

assumption_claims.statement: A finite family F of finite sets is union-closed iff for every A in F and every B in F, including the case A = B, the union A union B is a member of F. The empty set is permitted as a member of F. Closure is required for the union of any two members, which for finite F is equivalent to closure under the union of any nonempty subfamily.

The ground set is U(F), the union of all members of F. The word element ranges over U(F) and over nothing else; in particular it does not range over members of F. The frequency of x is freq_F(x) = card({A in F : x in A}), an exact nonnegative integer.

card(F) is the number of distinct members of F. When the empty set is a member it is counted, so the empty set contributes to card(F) while contributing to no frequency. This is the harder of the two counting conventions and it is frozen; the convention that excludes the empty set from card(F) is a different statement and is not claimed.

A linear 3-uniform generating system is a family G = {A_1, ..., A_m} with m >= 1 of pairwise distinct sets, each of cardinality exactly 3, such that card(A_i intersect A_j) <= 1 for all i != j. Its union-closure is F(G) = { union of A_i over i in S : S subset of {1,...,m} }, where the empty index set yields the empty set. The uniformity parameter is frozen at 3.
For any finite family G, the set of all unions of subfamilies of G is union-closed and contains the empty set, because the union of the union over S and the union over T is the union over S union T.

For every member of the frozen class, m >= 1 gives A_1 in F(G) with card(A_1) = 3, so the headline hypothesis that F has at least one nonempty member holds automatically and is never a live side condition inside the class.

When the m generators are pairwise disjoint, the 2^m subfamily unions are pairwise distinct, so card(F) = 2^m, and every x in U(F) lies in exactly the unions indexed by sets containing the single generator that contains x, giving freq_F(x) = 2^(m-1) = card(F)/2 for every x. The frozen inequality is therefore attained with equality inside the class and cannot be strengthened to a strict inequality.

When generators overlap, distinct index sets can have equal unions, so card(F) < 2^m in general. card(F) must be computed from the deduplicated canonical member set and never from 2^m. Example: the three 2-element generators of a triangle collapse three of eight unions into one, and the analogous collapse occurs for 3-element generators sharing points.

The planning dossier reports that Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture has extensive literature and a deceptively simple statement, creating high rediscovery and hidden-hypothesis risk. This is an untrusted planning-note statement. It is not acquired, not verified, and it is one of the claims the ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check must cover.

Unsourced recollection carried into this dossier and explicitly untrusted: the conjecture is reported settled for families containing a member of size one or two, for families realizable as lower semimodular lattices, for sufficiently small ground sets, and reported to have a general positive-fraction partial result below one half. None of these statements is acquired, quoted, or verified. Each must be revalidated under the ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check, and the frozen class must be compared against every one of them before the class is described as anything other than not_assessed.

Every frequency and family size on the trust path is an exact Python integer. The half condition is evaluated as the integer comparison 2 * freq_F(x) >= card(F), never as a division, a rational, or a floating-point ratio. Members are stored in one canonical encoding, sorted tuples of sorted ground-set labels, deduplicated before counting, and the whole canonical family is content-hashed so a claim names the exact object it was computed from. No floating-point value may appear on any trust path.

A reduction is admissible only with a proof that it preserves union closure and preserves the target property in the direction it is used. Preserving union closure alone is the standard trap: a map that sends a union-closed family to a union-closed family but can create a half-frequency element that the original lacked proves nothing about the original. Every reduction lemma must state its direction and be checked on the enumerated envelope as a falsifiability probe.

Weight-function and averaging arguments over union-closed families, and entropy or information-theoretic arguments toward a constant fraction, must not be re-derived blind. The planning dossier names rediscovery as the dominant risk for this item, so any such argument is treated as a rediscovery candidate until the ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check has run over it, and a bounded enumeration that agrees with such an argument is not evidence that the argument is new or correct.

formalization.statement: forall m in Z with m >= 1, forall G = {A_1,...,A_m} pairwise distinct sets with card(A_i) = 3 for all i and card(A_i intersect A_j) <= 1 for all i != j, let F = { union(A_i for i in S) : S subset of {1,...,m} } and U = union(A for A in F); then exists x in U with 2 * card({A in F : x in A}) >= card(F), where card(F) counts distinct members and includes the empty set obtained from S = empty
quantifiers: forall m an integer with m >= 1
forall G a family of m pairwise distinct 3-element sets with card(A_i intersect A_j) <= 1 for every i != j
forall S a subset of {1,...,m}, the union of A_i over i in S is a member of F, the empty S giving the empty set
exists x in U(F), the union of all members of F
forall A in F, membership of x in A is decided exactly

quantifier_mapping: every finite union-closed family F with at least one nonempty member
every F = F(G) for G a linear 3-uniform generating system with m >= 1 generators
there exists x in U(F), the union of all members of F
belonging to at least half of its sets
2 * freq_F(x) >= card(F) as an integer comparison
closed under the union of any two members, including a member with itself
definition_mapping: family closed under the union of any two members, empty set permitted as a member
element of the ground set U(F), the union of all members of F
number of distinct members of F, counting the empty set when it is a member
F is the union-closure of m >= 1 pairwise distinct 3-element sets with pairwise intersections of size at most one
assumption_delta: The headline conjecture assumes only union closure plus one nonempty member; the frozen target adds the linear 3-uniform generating condition, so it is a strict special case of the headline statement.
The uniformity parameter is frozen at 3; the statement for all k >= 2 simultaneously and the statement for k = 2 are separate targets and are not claimed here.
The empty set is admitted as a member and counted in card(F), which strengthens the burden relative to the convention that omits it.
No novelty is asserted for the frozen class; whether it is already covered by a published special case is not_assessed and is an acquisition question.
edge_case_delta: m = 1 gives F = {empty set, A_1}, card(F) = 2, and every x in A_1 has freq 1 = card(F)/2, so the bound holds with equality.
Pairwise disjoint generators give card(F) = 2^m and freq 2^(m-1) for every ground-set element, so equality is attained for arbitrarily large families inside the class.
The degenerate family F = {empty set} is outside the class because m >= 1 forces a 3-element member.
Overlapping generators make distinct index sets collapse to equal unions, so card(F) < 2^m and card(F) must be read off the deduplicated member set.
The empty member contributes to card(F) and to no frequency, so it acts against the claim and is deliberately retained.

success_criteria: a rigorous proof of the frozen target for the whole frozen class under the frozen conventions
an exact counterexample inside the frozen class, given as a canonical content-hashed family with exact integer frequencies and a replayed independent check
a proved reduction lemma that shrinks the frozen class to an exactly stated smaller class, with its preservation of union closure and of the target property proved in the direction used
or an explicit unresolved outcome that records the smallest remaining obligation
stopping_rules: stop on an exact certificate: a replayed counterexample family or a completed proof for the frozen class
stop when fresh model spend for this target reaches USD 20
stop when no proof obligation has been discharged and no new exclusion recorded for two consecutive review points

never promote exhaustion of the bounded enumeration envelope into the unrestricted universal claim, and never present the absence of a counterexample in the envelope as evidence for the headline conjecture
